'''''Vallisneria spiralis''''', also known as '''straight vallisneria''', '''tape grass''', or '''eel grass''' is a common [[aquarium]] plant that prefers good light and a nutrient rich [[Substrate (aquarium)|substrate]]. In the wild, it can be found in tropical and sub-tropical regions worldwide. 

==Overview==
It has narrow, [[leaf shape|linear]] [[leaves]] that range in colour from a pale-green to reddish up to 3 feet (1 m) long and up to 0.75 inches broad. ''V. spiralis'' is [[monoecious]] with male flowers carried on long spiral stalks that break away from the plant and float on the water's surface. In the variety ''V. s. gigantea'' the female flowers are on stalks ([[pedicels]]) up to six feet (1.85 meters) in length. After the female flowers have been [[pollinated]], the [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] curls up like a [[tendril]], drawing the young fruit closer to the bed of the stream or pond; thus the name "spiralis".<ref>{{cite book | last= Perry | first= Francis | date= 1961 | title= Water Gardening | location= London | publisher= Country Life | page= 172 }}</ref> Seeds have not been observed germinating in aquaria. Instead, it most often propagates by runners which can lead to dense stands.<ref name="d979">{{cite web | last=McElroy | first=Cory | title=Care Guide for Vallisneria – Our Favorite "One Plant Wonder" | website=Aquarium Co-Op | date=2017-01-31 | url=https://www.aquariumcoop.com/blogs/aquarium/vallisneria | access-date=2025-01-06}}</ref>.

It can be eaten when steamed or boiled.

[[File:1856aquariumfresh.png|thumb|center|''Vallisneria spiralis'' was already being used as an aquarium plant in 1856, as shown in this illustration from that time.]]

One [[form (botany)|form]] of this plant has been described: ''V. spiralis'' f. ''tortifolia'', which has also been elevated to the species level by some taxonomists under the name ''V. tortissima''. The form has tightly twisted leaves. Along with this form, many other trade names have been developed for small variations on the species. Their taxonomic status is uncertain.{{Cn|date=January 2021}}

==Invasive species==
The species is an effective invader due to its efficient dispersal, vegetative reproduction, high biomass production, and popularity in the aquarium trade.<ref name=":0" /> ''V. spiralis'' is an "unwanted organism" in [[New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biosecurity.govt.nz/pests/vallisneria-spiralis|title=Eelgrass|date=11 December 2008|publisher=MAF Biosecurity New Zealand|access-date=12 November 2010}}</ref> It is listed on the [[National Pest Plant Accord]] prohibiting it from sale and commercial propagation and distribution. Since 2013 ''V. spiralis'' has been listed as a [[alien species|naturalized alien]] in [[Iceland]], where it was recorded in geothermal ponds.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title = Vallisneria spiralis and Egeria densa (Hydrocharitaceae) in arctic and subarctic Iceland|last1 = Wasowicz|first1 = Pawel|date = 1 August 2014|journal = New Journal of Botany|doi = 10.1179/2042349714Y.0000000043|last2 = Przedpelska-Wasowicz|first2 = Ewa|last3 = Gudmundsdottir|first3 = Lara|last4 = Tamayo|first4 = Mariana|issue = 2|volume = 4|pages = 85–89| bibcode=2014NJBot...4...85W |s2cid = 85764375}}</ref>
